introduction.title: The Science Behind Your Report
introduction.subtitle: How DNA Analysis Works
introduction.snps_body: Your DNA contains 3 billion 'letters'. A Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) is a single-letter change (e.g., A to G) in that code. These variations are what we analyze to determine your unique biological tendencies.
introduction.gathering_body: By cross-referencing your SNPs with clinical research, we can determine the efficiency of specific enzymes (like EPHX1). This helps us see if a biological pathway is likely to be 'Fast', 'Slow', or 'Standard'.
introduction.limitations_body: DNA is your hardware, but lifestyle is your software. These results show your genetic potential; how you eat, sleep, and move determines how those genes are actually expressed (Epigenetics).

English.strength_summary_intro: While these traits did not trigger a deep dive, they represent significant genetic advantages.
English.risk_summary_intro: These traits did not trigger a detailed deep dive, but they represent areas of potential vulnerability.
English.inheritance_desc: This section visualizes where your active genetic traits originated.

introduction_education.section_1: This DNA-analyzer was created with the purpose of getting more value out of a MyHeritage test. I got the idea when I noticed that for a steep price, they offered to share a handful of impactful SNPs (Genes). In order to do that, it means they already have the result available from my DNA test. This made me feel somewhat exploited knowing they have my DNA and impactful information they are gatekeeping and might be passing on through some loophole in some fine print I failed to read. But I knew that they can't keep my data without a receipt, and that receipt is very valuable.
introduction_education.section_2a: Through some inside knowledge i also happen to know that DNA sequencing has become a lot cheaper and isn't as cumbersome as it previously used to be. Today they perform WGS (Whole Genome Sequencing), which means they get all of it, then decide what to keep and so much of it is worth keeping. So, I decided to build this product with that insight. How this product differ is that instead of testing 20 impactful genes as some other products do and they do offer a more refined product on those genes, this one tests over 200, including most, if not all, of the impactful genes and some might be less impactful, but toghether with other genes they form a chain of downstream and upstream effects.
introduction_education.section_2b: But this product isn't perfect. It is made by one person (me), and it's only feasible due to the training and high performance of the best AI research models. They accumulate the data and populate my own genomic library. This data isn't easily digestible however and I can't stress this enough: ONLY due to rigorous guardrails, repeated sanitization, and logic gating could this data even be assembled and that data itself isn't perfect, in fact fighting the hallucinations(AI lying or being confused by the data) has been the main struggle. But even though it's not a perfect product, it is the best bang-for-the-buck, return-on-investment DNA test that I could find on the market. It's also a product I made for myself, my friends, and my family.
introduction_education.section_3: Now with all of that out of the way, here are some fundamental things you need to understand before diving into your results. that aren't obvious
introduction_education.bullet_1: **1. Evolutionary Optimization:** You are a collection of genetic strengths accumulated over your lineage. You aren't a fragile 50/50 split of strengths and weaknesses, but rather **80% strengths, 15% risks, and 5% vulnerabilities** (we'll touch more on this later).
introduction_education.bullet_2: **2. Ancestral Context:** You have unique mutations that exist specifically to solve problems from environmental pressures your ancestors used to face. What causes an issue today was likely a survival mechanism yesterday.
introduction_education.bullet_3: **3. Highly Interconnected:** Your DNA consists of blueprints for how to solve things, and they are highly interconnected. One individual gene isn't enough to tell the whole tale, but together they form a complete picture.
introduction_education.section_4: To understand your results, you need to know two key terms: GoF (Gain of Function) and LoF (Loss of Function). GoF makes a gene work faster, meaning it is allocated more resources and excels at its task. LoF means the opposite—the gene receives fewer resources and works slower than average. Typically, these genes operate at a percentage of normal baseline functionality, such as running at 50% (LoF) versus 200% (GoF) capacity.
introduction_education.section_5: Think of your DNA as the blueprint for a factory floor. Your body takes in raw materials (building blocks provided by the food you eat) and converts them through complex assembly lines into the products needed to survive and thrive. When a system operates at a GoF or LoF capacity, it is rarely a mistake—it is usually an adaptation to an environment your ancestors had to overcome. For example, consider the rs5400/SLC2A2 gene, which regulates how well your brain senses sugar intake. Centuries ago, when calories were scarce, an LoF here was a massive survival asset because it kept you hungry and motivated to forage. Today, in an environment of modern abundance, that same LoF is a liability that heavily increases the risk of obesity and diabetes. The gene itself doesn't magically create fat; it simply sabotages your brain's fullness gauge on the factory floor. It does this by dropping the signal, only transmitting every third caloric alert onward to the brain.
introduction_education.section_6: Generally speaking, GoF tends to be a positive, but it is heavily contextualized. Let's take the gene rs40184/SLC6A3 (DAT1), which handles how quickly dopamine is cleared from your system. If you have CC, it means you have a GoF on this gene and your brain will clear out dopamine faster, while a TT means you have an LoF and your brain will clear out dopamine slower. This has a massive impact on your motivation. A GoF here is highly associated with ADHD, because the chemistry required to motivate you to stick with one task, one thought is making that motivational signal significantly weaker than for someone else.
introduction_education.section_7: This brings us to upstream and downstream effects, which act as the interconnected assembly line in our factory analogy. We will use alcohol metabolism as an example. When you take a drink, ethanol enters your body and hits your brain's reward system. Here, upstream genes like OPRM1 and GABRB3 determine how much dopamine is released and how strong the mood-altering effect will be. Meanwhile, your liver begins breaking down the ethanol into a highly toxic byproduct called acetaldehyde. The ADH1B gene controls the speed of this station. If you have the CC genotype, the conversion is steady. But if you have the TT genotype, you have a GoF that runs this conversion incredibly fast, rapidly flooding your system with toxins. Finally, the downstream ALDH2 gene must clear that toxic acetaldehyde by converting it into harmless acetate. If you have the GA or AA genotype here, you have an LoF. Your assembly line moves very slowly, meaning you are quite literally poisoned while waiting for your body to slowly trickle the toxins away. Together, these genes form a complete chain where a fast upstream GoF paired with a slow downstream LoF creates a massive, painful pile-up on the factory floor.
introduction_education.section_8: Previously i mentioned how you consist of 80% strengths, 15% risk and 5% vulnerabilities. The ethanol conversion chain is a great example of this, now imagine that you have the fast conversion of Ethanol>Acetaldehyde and the slow conversion of Acetaldehyde>Acetate leading to Acetaldehyde toxins building up fast in your system and then lingering, this makes you highly susceptible to acute alcohol poisoning. Two teenagers can drink the same amount, but one is at much greater risk. This creates a huge vulnerability that sits like a ticking bomb, just waiting to go off at first discovery, but by studying and understanding these upstream/downstream pathways coupled with GoF and LoF we can map out these vulnerabilities and improve our quality of life as well as avoiding damaging/life threatening circumstances.
introduction_education.section_9: Understanding these pathways brings us to the frontier of genetic science. It explains why a biological stressor your 20-year-old self could easily brush off can become fatal decades later. The answer is cumulative damage. Every human possesses what we might call a death pattern a statistical likelihood of breaking down in a specific way, often mirroring your parents and grandparents. Evolution designed your genetic strengths to keep you thriving just long enough to reproduce and raise offspring. After that, your unique GoF and LoF combinations dictate where your factory machinery will fail first, whether that leans toward cardiovascular disease, Alzheimer's, cancer, or metabolic dysfunction. These vulnerabilities are all competing to be the ultimate breaking point. However, the goal of this report is not to stave off death, but to maximize your healthspan the years you live free from chronic pain and disease. By identifying your unique death pattern now, you can actively reinforce your weakest biological pathways before they fail.
introduction_education.section_10: Let us investigate a specific GoF-LoF-GoF chain to see how these patterns hide in plain sight. Upstream, you may have an aggressive GoF in the SOD2 gene (rs4880), meaning your body is exceptionally efficient at neutralizing free radicals before they ever reach your cells. However, the middle of this assembly line has a severe LoF in the GSTP1 gene (rs1695). Your cellular structures are biologically fragile and lack the standard protection to conjugate and clear toxins if they manage to bypass the first line. Finally, your downstream station has another powerful GoF in the TP53 gene (rs1042522), a high-stringency quality control mechanism known as the guardian of the genome. It ruthlessly identifies and deletes any cell with a copying error before it can multiply. In this specific pattern, you are functionally shielded under normal conditions; your GoF strengths act as massive buffers that ensure the fragile LoF in the center is never truly tested. Now, imagine a habit like smoking is introduced. Your GoF genes work overtime to maintain the shield, but eventually, you hit a threshold you cannot handle. Poor nutrition, lack of sleep, and a sudden infection weaken these overworked pathways, and the floodgates open. Cancer begins forming rapidly, and even if the defense gap only exists for five days, that is enough time for it to establish a foothold. Because your body bet its genetic capital on prevention rather than active containment, you are left exposed to a runaway threat it was never designed to fight in this way.
introduction_education.section_11: I created this product because these insights provide an undeniable advantage to anyone who accesses them, including myself and my family. To me, genomics is the ultimate frontier because it is quite literally code, code we can decipher with functions to read and learn from. The fact that just four bases Adenine (A), Cytosine (C), Guanine (G), and Thymine (T) can combine in triplets to create 64 possible combinations that produce all 20 amino acids is a feat of engineering that beggars belief. Even more fascinating is that among these 64 combinations, specific sequences act as precise functional commands like 'stop' or 'end of translation.' . I suggest that you use this as a starting point to make some changes in your life, but also as a introduction to the topic. Don't stop here, go explore how it works in detail and reap even more benefit
introduction_education.section_12: Who are you truly? You are looking at the answer. This code is your essence, and regardless of the strengths or vulnerabilities you find within it, you are unique and magnificent. It is remarkable to consider what your ancestors endured to pass down this blueprint; every downregulated pathway and every specific trait was a calculated survival strategy, your survival strategy. Even an autoimmune sensitivity can be a hidden strength; that same hyper-vigilance might be the very trait that allows you to survive a viral threat that reaps a whole populations of others. Your DNA is not a list of errors; it is a record of resilience, showing exactly how your lineage survived the past so you can thrive. I hope your results will be interesting and lead to many aha moments, laughter and deepd-ives, it did for me and my spouse as well, since it turns out our psychology was well mirrored by our findings

introduction.title: Vetenskapen bakom din rapport
introduction.subtitle: Hur DNA-analys fungerar
introduction.snps_body: Ditt DNA består av 3 miljarder 'bokstäver'. En Single Nucleotide Polymorphism (SNP) är en ändring av en enstaka bokstav (t.ex. A till G). Det är dessa variationer vi analyserar för att förstå dina unika biologiska tendenser.
introduction.gathering_body: Genom att korsreferera dina SNPs med klinisk forskning kan vi fastställa effektiviteten hos specifika enzymer (som EPHX1). Detta hjälper oss att se om en biologisk process sannolikt är 'Snabb', 'Långsam' eller 'Standard'.
introduction.limitations_body: DNA är din hårdvara, men livsstilen är din mjukvara. Dessa resultat visar din genetiska potential; hur du äter, sover och rör dig avgör hur dessa gener faktiskt uttrycks (Epigenetik).

Swedish.strength_summary_intro: Dessa egenskaper utlöste inte en djupanalys, men representerar betydande genetiska fördelar.
Swedish.risk_summary_intro: Dessa egenskaper utlöste inte en detaljerad djupanalys, men representerar områden av potentiell sårbarhet.
